transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Veridian - Head of Data), Ethan Rowe (Veridian - Security Architect), Priya Singh (Veridian - ML Eng)

High-level summary (auto):
POC scoping focused on data handling requirements for an inference POC: what counts as PII, options for disabling/stubbing logs, retention TTLs, prompt storage, and whether a hosted vs dedicated/private deployment is required given regulated health data. Team agreed to run micro-benchmarks and exchange redacted prompts and SOC2 + KMS docs.

Topics flagged: PII redaction, audit logs, prompt storage, retention overrides, KMS/HSM, VPC/private deployment, micro-benchmark sizing, success criteria for POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex and Samira from Redwood, and from Veridian Maria, Ethan, Priya?
[00:05] Maria (Customer): Yeah, hi — thanks. We have about 45 minutes blocked. Main thing, we need to understand how you handle PII during an evaluation and what options exist to prevent prompt data being persisted in logs.
[00:12] Samira (Redwood SE): Absolutely. We'll start with an overview and then dig into options. Quick note: our transcription may not be perfect, sorry for any misnames.
[00:18] Priya (Customer - ML Eng): No worries. For context, our dataset includes clinical notes and some patient identifiers in a few fields — for the POC we can provide a redacted subset, but legal wants to understand audit trails and retention first.
[00:28] Ethan (Customer - Sec): And we need to know whether Redwood stores prompts or whether we can opt-out or mask certain fields. Also interested in KMS + HSM options and TLS at rest/encryption.
[00:36] Alex: Right. High level: for a hosted Redwood POC we have three levers — logging enabled (default for diagnostics), logging with PII redaction pipeline, or logging disabled (no request/response persisted). Then there's Dedicated/Private where the control plane is customer VPC and logs never leave your environment.
[00:50] Maria: When you say "logging disabled" — do you mean absolutely nothing is written to disk? What about metrics/latency traces?
[00:57] Samira: Great question. "Logging disabled" for request/response means we won't persist prompt text or generated completions. Service-level metrics (like token counts, latency histograms, error rates) are still collected in aggregated form for SLO monitoring, but we can configure them to be non-identifying. If you want absolutely zero telemetry, that's only feasible in Private/on-prem or with very strict Dedicated options — but that also limits our ability to debug.
[01:24] Maria: Ok. We probably need aggregated metrics only. We can't have full prompts in logs.
[01:28] Ethan: Also, do you do field-level redaction or tokenization? We need the option to replace patient name fields client-side before sending. But we'd like a server-side fallback if the client misses something.
[01:37] Samira: There are two approaches we recommend: 1) pre-send client-side redaction — pushdown the sensitive fields (we provide a reference regex-based sanitizer), and 2) a server-side PII redaction pipeline that can be enabled for the POC. Server-side uses a best-effort NER-based scrubber plus configurable allowlists/blocklists and hashing for replaced tokens. Important caveat: automated redaction isn't 100% perfect — that's why we often recommend both layers.
[02:02] Priya: Will redaction modify the prompt that the model actually sees? We need to know for quality measurement — if we hash names are we changing model semantics?
[02:09] Samira: Right — hashed tokens change semantics. For evaluation you might want a synthetic deterministic substitution scheme: we replace real names with consistent tokens (e.g., PERSON_1) so meaning is preserved across examples. We can support that in our POC pipeline.
[02:21] Alex: To tie to success criteria — sounds like Veridian's primary gates are: a) security signoff (SOC2 + KMS attestations), b) ability to run with logs scrubbed or disabled, c) benchmark meeting latency and throughput targets with real-ish prompts, and d) acceptable impact on model quality after redaction.
[02:36] Maria: Yes, and add e) retention controls — legal wants audit logs but with strict TTL windows (like 30 days max for any request flows), and ability to purge on demand.
[02:45] Samira: We support per-customer retention TTLs for hosted POC, and for Dedicated you can set retention to zero or have logs routed to your S3 with lifecycle policies. Our platform also offers immediate purge APIs that delete stored prompts and completions — we will include details in the security artifact.
[02:58] Ethan: About prompt storage — do you persist prompts for prompt-tuning / cache warmups or KV caches? I'm worried about prefix caching keeping user data in memory/disk beyond a request.
[03:06] Samira: We use a combination of in-memory KV caches for active sessions and optional persistent prefix caches for performance. Persistent caches are configurable and disabled by default in POCs with sensitive data; in-memory cache exists only for the duration of the request lifecycle and is not written to disk unless you enable persistent caching.
[03:23] Maria: Good. For the POC we want persistent caching off and no prompt storage. Also we want prompt telemetry turned off except anonymized token counts.
[03:30] Alex: Noted. On the benchmarking side, to scope the micro-benchmark Samira, any recommendations?
[03:35] Samira: For throughput/latency we suggest two model variants (a smaller open model and a medium instruction-tuned model) to simulate both cost and quality tradeoffs. Run these scenarios: 1) 512-token sequences at 10 QPS sustained for 30 minutes; 2) 2048-token tail-latency test with bursts to 2-3x expected QPS for 10 minutes; and 3) mixed prompt distribution with 20% long-form and 80% short prompts. We'll measure p50/p90/p99 latency, GPU mem utilization, token/s cost and KV cache hits. We'll also capture sample outputs to validate quality post-redaction.
[04:12] Priya: That sounds reasonable. Our estimated POC workload is about 8 QPS average with spikes to 25 during business hours; average seq length ~400 tokens. We need to confirm the Dedicated sizing you recommend for sustained 8 QPS at 400 tokens.
[04:24] Samira: We'll size that in the micro-benchmark. Ballpark: one A100-like GPU can handle X tokens/s depending on batching and quantization; we'll produce a recommended config (batch sizes, batching windows) and show expected cost. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity and autoscale for spikes.
[04:39] Maria: Back to compliance — is there an audit log with per-request metadata fields? Our legal requires user_id (hashed), timestamp, route/model version, tokens_in/tokens_out, and whether any redaction occurred.
[04:50] Alex: Yes, audit logs can include those fields. For hosted POC we can redact user_id and provide hashed user_id, and include a boolean field 'redaction_applied'. We can also enable a separate immutable audit stream to your S3 bucket if you choose Dedicated or Private.
[05:02] Ethan: And about KMS — do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:05] Samira: Yes. For Dedicated/Private we support CMKs via AWS KMS and bring-your-own HSM integrations. For hosted POC we can also support envelope encryption with customer-supplied keys in limited cases; we'll detail that in the security docs.
[05:16] Maria: Great. What's the typical timeline for the POC if we start next week?
[05:20] Alex: Suggested timeline: week 1 — security review and exchange docs + produce redacted prompt set; week 2 — environment setup (hosted config or Dedicated provisioning) + Samira runs micro-benchmark; week 3 — run customer sample workload, collect quality/eval metrics and iterate; week 4 — wrap-up, remediation steps, and decision. So roughly 3–4 weeks.
[05:36] Priya: Are there any blockers on your side for the micro-benchmark? We might need a small dataset with labels to evaluate quality.
[05:43] Samira: We'll need: redacted prompts, expected outputs or scoring rubric, and an agreed-upon set of prompts that include edge PII cases. Also let us know the SLOs — e.g., p95 < 350ms for short prompts — otherwise we'll default to your stated average latency target.
[05:58] Maria: Legal wants to see the purge API in action before signing off. Can you demo that?
[06:02] Alex: Yes, we can schedule a short demo to show purge + retention TTL flows. We'll include an audit trail of purge requests in the demo.
[06:09] Ethan: One more question: do you keep prompt embeddings, or do you generate embeddings for logs? Embeddings could be considered sensitive too.
[06:16] Samira: Good call — embeddings are persisted only if you enable the embeddings index feature. For the POC, we will keep embeddings disabled. If you need semantic search later we can work on hashed or client-side stored indexes.
[06:28] Maria: I'm also concerned about transcript capture — will Fireflies transcripts be available externally? (laugh)
[06:33] Alex: Ha — Fireflies is a separate service; for the POC we won't share internal transcripts beyond the participants.
[06:38] Priya: Ok. Anything else on success criteria? To recap: security signoff, no persisted PII in logs, ability to purge, benchmark results within latency/throughput targets, and preservation of quality after redaction.
[06:50] Alex: Yep. Also request that you sign an NDA or addendum about handling sample data for the POC; we'll attach the standard POC addendum to the SOW.
[06:58] Maria: We'll loop legal. One last technical thing — are there pre-built redaction regex templates for PHI/SSNs?
[07:04] Samira: We have a zero-configuration PHI template that covers common US formats (SSN, MRN, DOB patterns) and a configurable NER model for non-structured cases. We will share the template and you can run it client-side prior to sending.
[07:16] Ethan: Perfect. Let's capture next steps.
[07:19] Alex: I'll follow up with the SOC2 pack, KMS notes, and the PII redaction template by Tuesday the 18th. Samira will run the micro-benchmark and share results by the 21st. Maria/Ethan will send the redacted prompts and retention requirements by the 17th. We'll schedule a VPC deep-dive after that.
[07:35] Maria: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:37] Alex: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript. Notes: occasional transcription errors present; speaker labels may have minor mismatches.
